_**User (2026-09-17 18:44:35Z)**_

Hey Claude, I would like to implement a new feature for the project. This is the issue name: Copy link button isn't properly shown in the user's selected language #45: Issue Summary
As a user who uses a different language, when I copy the link for an event in the event summary page, I get a properly translated message response. However, if I copy the link from a specific event edit page, the pop-up alert that shows up is not translated properly.

Steps to Reproduce
Open website
Have a language other than English selected
Click a specific event to open its edit page
Click the copy link button in the top right and observe the message that appears in the bottom center.
Actual Results
User receives an English message notifying them that their link has been copied, regardless of language setting.
Expected Results
Message notifying user that their link is copied should be properly set to the language they defined in the settings. First, I am tasked with doing a manual concept location; I am already familiar with this area of the code (the event-type page) from previous bug fix investigations. I originally asked for help with understanding the basics of how the React components are stored in general, which led me to look at apps/web/modules (AI helped me get here), then I saw there was a /event-types folder. From there I looked through the files until I stumbled upon a familiar line of text "Link copied!", which told me I was in the right area. It turns out that in trying to solve the previous bug, I had already stumbled upon the file of the present issue. My hypothesis (which you should verify), is that the cause of the language bug is in /apps/web/modules/event-types/EventTypeLayout.tsx, specifically any line with the text "showToast("Link copied!", "success");". My understanding (from a working version of this same button found in apps\web\modules\event-types\views\event-types-listing-view.tsx, is that there is supposed to be a translation lookup function instead of the raw string: "showToast(t("link_copied"), "success");". Did I correctly perform the concept location?

Yes — your concept location is correct, with one small path correction.

**Confirmed:**
- The file is `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx` (note: it's in the `components/` subfolder, not directly under `event-types/` as you wrote — easy to mix up).
- It has **two** occurrences of the hardcoded string, both at fault:
  - Line 182 — the icon button in the top-right button group
  - Line 238 — the "Copy link" item in the `⋮` dropdown menu (for smaller screens)
- Your fix hypothesis is exactly right: `showToast("Link copied!", "success")` → `showToast(t("link_copied"), "success")`, matching the working pattern in `event-types-listing-view.tsx:641/775`.
- The `link_copied` key already exists in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`, so no new translation entry is needed — you're just wiring up the existing key.
- I also confirmed `t` is already used elsewhere in this same component (e.g. `t("copy_link")`, `t("embed")`, `t("delete")` nearby), so it's already in scope — the fix is a pure string swap, no new imports needed.

One thing to check before you edit: confirm `t` in scope at both call sites is the same `useLocale()`/`i18n` translation function already used for `t("copy_link")` right next to each broken line (it clearly is, based on the surrounding code), so both fixes are drop-in replacements.

## Findings

**1. Existing tests for EventTypeLayout.tsx**
None. `find . -iname "EventTypeLayout*"` returns only the component itself (`apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`), no `.test.tsx` sibling. No test file for `event-types-listing-view.tsx` either. The repo uses **Vitest** + **React Testing Library** (`@testing-library/react`) everywhere — no enzyme. Config: `vitest.config.mts` at repo root.

**2. `showToast`**
Imported as `import { showToast } from "@calcom/ui/components/toast";` (same in `EventTypeLayout.tsx:21`). Standard mocking pattern seen across the repo (e.g. `packages/platform/atoms/event-types/__tests__/EventTypeListItem.test.tsx:26-28`, `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/tabs/advanced/FormBuilder.test.tsx:38-40`):
```ts
vi.mock("@calcom/ui/components/toast", () => ({
  showToast: vi.fn(),
}));
```
Then assert with `expect(showToast).toHaveBeenCalledWith("expected-value", "success")`.

**3. Mocking `t`/`useLocale`**
Universal pattern across the codebase (11 test files, e.g. `EventTypeListItem.test.tsx:19-23`, `UserDropdown.test.tsx:9-13`) is an **identity mock**:
```ts
vi.mock("@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale", () => ({
  useLocale: () => ({ t: (key: string) => key }),
}));
```
Tests then assert the **i18n key** is used, not a real translated string (e.g. `expect(showToast).toHaveBeenCalledWith("link_copied", "success")`). I found no test anywhere in the repo that mocks a non-English locale to render actual translated text — that pattern does not currently exist. For this bug, the idiomatic repo-consistent test is: mock `t` to return the key (or a distinguishable marker string), click copy-link, and assert `showToast` was called with `"link_copied"` (the key) rather than the literal `"Link copied!"`. That alone proves the fix without needing real i18n resource loading. If you want to go further and prove a genuinely translated string appears, you'd need to introduce a new pattern (e.g. mock `t` as `(key) => (key === "link_copied" ? "Enlace copiado!" : key)`), which has no precedent in the repo but is straightforward to add.

**4. Component weight**
`EventTypeLayout.tsx` (function `EventTypeSingleLayout`) is heavy: props include `eventType`, `currentUserMembership`, `team`, `formMethods: UseFormReturn<FormValues>` (react-hook-form), `tabsNavigation`, plus renders `WebShell` (`@calcom/web/modules/shell/Shell`), `PlatformShell`, `EventTypeEmbedButton`/`EventTypeEmbedDialog`, and `DeleteDialog`. It has no direct tRPC hook calls itself, but its Shell/embed/dialog children likely do. There is no dedicated test-utils/wrapper file for this component (checked, none found; only unrelated `test-utils.tsx` in `packages/features/bookings/Booker/__tests__/`). Existing analogous tests (`FormBuilder.test.tsx:47-63`) build an ad-hoc `Wrapper` with `useForm()` + `<FormProvider>` and `vi.mock` each heavy import individually (auto-animate, next/navigation, toast, prisma) rather than using a shared harness — you'd need to do the same: mock `WebShell`, `PlatformShell`, `EventTypeEmbedButton`/`Dialog`, `DeleteDialog`, and `useLocale`/`showToast`, and wrap in a real or stubbed `formMethods` (`useForm()` result satisfies `UseFormReturn<FormValues>` loosely, or pass a minimal mock object with `getValues`).

**5. `event-types-listing-view.tsx` working case**
Confirmed correct usage at lines 641 (`showToast(t("link_copied"), "success")`), 654 (`private_link_copied`), and 775 (`link_copied` again), plus `MultiplePrivateLinksController.tsx:284`. No test file exists for `event-types-listing-view.tsx` to mirror — you'd be establishing the first test for this exact assertion pattern in the codebase, though the `showToast`+`useLocale` identity-mock idiom from `EventTypeListItem.test.tsx`/`FormBuilder.test.tsx` is the direct template to reuse.

```markdown
# Fix: Copy-link toast not translated in event-type edit page (Issue #45)

## Context

On the event-type **edit** page, clicking the copy-link button (desktop icon button, and its duplicate in the mobile `⋮` dropdown) shows a hardcoded English toast — `"Link copied!"` — instead of the translated message. The same action on the event-types **listing** page correctly uses `t("link_copied")`. Concept location is confirmed: both bad call sites live in `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`.

The user wants a TDD-style workflow: write a failing unit test first, commit it, then make the one-line-per-callsite fix, commit that, run the full suite, then finish with lint/format and a PR. No e2e test is needed — this is a small, self-contained unit-testable change.

## Findings from investigation

- **Two broken call sites**, both in `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`:
  - Line 182 — desktop icon button (`StartIcon="link"`, inside `ButtonGroup`)
  - Line 238 — mobile `⋮` dropdown's "Copy link" `DropdownItem`
- **Working reference pattern** in `apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx:641,775`: `showToast(t("link_copied"), "success")`. The i18n key `link_copied` already exists in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json` — no new translation entries needed.
- **No existing test file** for `EventTypeLayout.tsx`. It's a heavy component: it imports `WebShell` (`@calcom/web/modules/shell/Shell`), `PlatformShell` (`packages/platform/atoms/src/components/ui/shell`), `EventTypeEmbedButton`/`EventTypeEmbedDialog`, and `DeleteDialog`, all of which pull in tRPC/other providers we don't want in a unit test.
- **Repo-wide i18n test convention** (confirmed in `EventTypeListItem.test.tsx`, `FormBuilder.test.tsx`): `useLocale` is mocked as an identity function (`t: (key) => key`), and assertions check that the **i18n key** was passed, not real translated text. There is no precedent for rendering actual per-locale strings — we will follow the existing convention rather than invent a new one (per user's decision).
  - This is sufficient to prove the fix: before the fix, `showToast` is called with the literal `"Link copied!"`; after the fix, it's called with `"link_copied"` (the key `t()` receives). A test asserting `showToast` was called with `"link_copied"` fails on current code and passes after the fix.
- **`showToast` mocking convention**: `vi.mock("@calcom/ui/components/toast", () => ({ showToast: vi.fn() }))`, then `expect(showToast).toHaveBeenCalledWith("link_copied", "success")`.
- **Selecting the buttons in the test**: the sibling "preview" button already has `data-testid="preview-button"` (line 162) for exactly this purpose. Neither the copy-link icon button nor the dropdown item has a `data-testid` today, and their accessible name isn't derived from the `tooltip` prop (tooltip content isn't wired to `aria-label`), so `getByRole` by name won't reliably find them. **Both `Button` and `DropdownItem` forward arbitrary props (including `data-testid`) to the underlying element**, so we'll add `data-testid="copy-link-button"` and `data-testid="copy-link-dropdown-item"` to the two elements, mirroring the existing `preview-button` convention. This is test scaffolding, not behavior, so it goes in the test commit, keeping the fix commit a pure 2-line swap.

## Implementation Plan

### Commit 1 — Add failing test (+ minimal test-support attributes)

1. In `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`, add `data-testid="copy-link-button"` to the icon `Button` at line ~172-184, and `data-testid="copy-link-dropdown-item"` to the `DropdownItem` at line ~232-242. (No other changes to this file in this commit.)
2. Create `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.test.tsx` (Vitest + React Testing Library, matching `FormBuilder.test.tsx` conventions):
   - `vi.mock("@calcom/ui/components/toast", () => ({ showToast: vi.fn() }))`
   - `vi.mock("@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale", () => ({ useLocale: () => ({ t: (key: string) => key }) }))`
   - Stub out heavy children so only the buttons under test matter:
     - `vi.mock("@calcom/web/modules/shell/Shell", ...)` → simple component rendering `props.CTA` and `props.children`
     - `vi.mock("../../../../../packages/platform/atoms/src/components/ui/shell", ...)` (the `PlatformShell` import path) → same simple stub
     - `vi.mock("@calcom/web/modules/embed/components/EventTypeEmbed", ...)` → stub `EventTypeEmbedButton`/`EventTypeEmbedDialog` as `null`
     - `vi.mock("./dialogs/DeleteDialog", ...)` → stub `DeleteDialog` as `null`
   - Build minimal props: a `formMethods` from real `useForm<FormValues>()` (via a small wrapper component) seeded with `defaultValues` covering what the component reads via `getValues`/`watch` (`users: [{ username: "test-user" }]`, `slug: "test-event"`, `schedulingType: null`, `hidden: false`, `metadata: {}`), plus minimal `eventType`, `bookerUrl`, `tabsNavigation: []`, `onDelete: vi.fn()`, `isUserOrganizationAdmin: false`.
   - Two test cases:
     - Clicking `getByTestId("copy-link-button")` calls `showToast` with `("link_copied", "success")` (not `"Link copied!"`).
     - Clicking `getByTestId("copy-link-dropdown-item")` calls `showToast` with `("link_copied", "success")`.
   - Run the test and confirm it **fails** against current code (proves it's a valid regression test).
3. Commit: `test: add regression test for translated copy-link toast (#45)`

### Commit 2 — Fix the bug

1. In `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`:
   - Line 182: `showToast("Link copied!", "success")` → `showToast(t("link_copied"), "success")`
   - Line 238: same swap
2. Re-run the new test file to confirm it now passes.
3. Commit: `fix: translate copy-link toast on event-type edit page (#45)`
```

```tsx
  color="secondary"
  data-testid="preview-button"
  target="_blank"
  variant="icon"
  href={permalink}
  rel="noreferrer"
  StartIcon="external-link"
/>
```

**2. The sibling file, `event-types-listing-view.tsx`**, uses the same pattern for its own preview button (`data-testid="preview-link-button"`, line 626) and elsewhere for dropdown triggers/items (`event-type-options-${type.id}`, `event-type-duplicate-${type.id}`, etc.).

**3. A real unit test consumes exactly this pattern** — `packages/platform/atoms/event-types/__tests__/EventTypeListItem.test.tsx:120`:
```tsx
const dropdownTrigger = screen.getByTestId("event-type-options-1");
expect(dropdownTrigger).toBeInTheDocument();
```

One caveat worth noting: I checked, and interestingly the *working* copy-link button in `event-types-listing-view.tsx:636` has **no** `data-testid` either — only its sibling preview button does. So there's no existing testid specifically on a "copy link" button to reuse verbatim, but the convention of adding one to make a button testable is clearly standard here, not something I'm inventing.

Given that, adding `data-testid="copy-link-button"` / `data-testid="copy-link-dropdown-item"` is the right call — no better alternative exists (tooltip text isn't wired to `aria-label`, so role/name queries won't work). describe("EventTypeSingleLayout - copy link toast translation", () => {
```typescript
  beforeEach(() => {
    vi.clearAllMocks();
    Object.defineProperty(navigator, "clipboard", {
      value: { writeText: vi.fn() },
      configurable: true,

    render(<TestHarness />);

});
```

```markdown
## What does this PR do?

On the event-type **edit** page, the copy-link controls (the desktop icon button and the "Copy link" item in the mobile `⋮` dropdown) called `showToast("Link copied!", "success")` with a hardcoded English string instead of the translated `link_copied` i18n key. As a result, users with a non-English language selected saw an untranslated toast after copying the link, even though the equivalent action on the event-types **listing** page already showed the correctly translated message.

This PR swaps both hardcoded strings for `t("link_copied")` in `apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.tsx`, matching the working pattern already used in `apps/web/modules/event-types/views/event-types-listing-view.tsx`. No new translation key was needed since `link_copied` already exists in `packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json`.

A regression test was added first (and confirmed to fail against the old code) before making the fix. Two `data-testid` attributes (`copy-link-button`, `copy-link-dropdown-item`) were also added to the affected elements so the test can target them directly, following the existing `preview-button` testid convention already present in the same file.

- Fixes #45

## Visual Demo (For contributors especially)

_Not captured as part of this change — the fix is a non-visual, one-line-per-callsite string swap (the toast text itself is the only user-visible difference, and only under a non-English locale). Happy to add a before/after screenshot on request._

## How should this be tested?

- No special environment variables are needed.
- Minimal test data: any event type you can open the edit page for.
- **Automated:** run `TZ=UTC yarn vitest run apps/web/modules/event-types/components/EventTypeLayout.test.tsx`. Two tests cover this fix — one for the desktop icon button, one for the mobile dropdown item — each asserting `showToast` is called with the `link_copied` i18n key instead of the literal string `"Link copied!"`.
- **Manual (happy path):**
  1. Set your account language to a non-English language.
  2. Open any event type's edit page.
  3. Click the copy-link icon button in the top-right button group (or, on a narrow viewport, open the `⋮` menu and click "Copy link").
  4. Expected: the confirmation toast at the bottom center appears in the selected language, not English.
- No e2e tests reference this toast text or these buttons today, so none are affected by this change.
```
